Live demo · Security and AI

Access that knows it’s really you.

This is what a topic like multi-modal biometric authentication becomes. Face, fingerprint and a live challenge, fused into one decision.

Face ID
Facial recognition
Finding your face
Build this as my project

1. Challenge-response

The server picks a random sequence, like turn left then right. A photo or a pre-recorded clip cannot know it in advance.

2. Signed, single-use sessions

Every attempt gets its own token, rate-limited and used once. A quality gate rejects blurry, dark or off-centre frames before matching.

3. Face match

YuNet finds the face and SFace turns it into an embedding, both as ONNX models running on OpenCV.

4. Fusion and floors

Face and fingerprint scores combine into one score, and each must also clear its own floor.

5. Decision, with a reason

Every grant or denial carries a reason code. The attempt log is hash-chained and tamper-evident, templates are encrypted, and raw images are never stored.

Under the hood · For engineers

The engineering behind the demo.

A real system, not a mock-up: built, tested on a phone in Zaria, and iterated until it held up.

What the server sees: five landmarks, a yaw estimate and a 128-d embedding score.

91automated tests
2ONNX models on OpenCV
5landmarks give head pose
1×use signed sessions
Phone camera -> quality gate (blur, light, centre) | v YuNet: face box + 5 landmarks ----> head-pose yaw | | v v SFace: 128-d embedding random challenge: left / right | | v | cosine match vs encrypted template | +---------------+-------------------+ v score fusion + per-modality floors v GRANTED / DENIED + reason code -> hash-chained log

Liveness from geometry

Yaw is the nose offset from the eye midpoint, divided by eye distance. A turn counts when the head leaves the target pose and then reaches it, so a fast left-to-right sweep still passes.

Security by design

  • HMAC-signed, single-use sessions
  • 5 failed attempts trigger a 60-second lockout
  • Replays are logged and denied
  • Templates encrypted, raw frames never stored
  • Attempt log is hash-chained and tamper-evident

Field-tested, then fixed

We recorded real attempts on a phone and fixed what broke: turn detection that needed a pause at centre, camera capture that stalled during network round trips, and stray requests after a decision. The final runs granted access repeatedly, with face scores around 0.9 against a 0.6 fusion threshold.

Honest limits

A phone browser cannot read a fingerprint sensor, so the demo labels its fingerprint as simulated on screen. The five-landmark backend supports left and right turns only, and this is a research build, not a certified anti-spoofing product.
